book: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology, 4th ed. (Rizzo)
kicker: Lesson 8 of your course, built from Chapter 8 of your Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology textbook (Rizzo). Test practice uses checked answers, because there is no official key for this test.

steps.title: What a joint is
teach: An articulation, or joint, is any place where two or more bones meet, whatever the amount of movement. Skull sutures are joints as much as the knee is.

Joints are classified by how much they move (function) and by what holds them together (structure) into three groups: synarthroses (no movement), amphiarthroses (slight movement) and diarthroses (free movement).

items.label: Diarthroses (synovial)
items.detail: Free movement: six types, like the hip and knee.

mnemonic.cue: SYN = sealed, AMPHI = a little, DI = do anything
mnemonic.explanation: Synarthroses don’t move, amphiarthroses move a little, diarthroses move freely.

act.prompt: How much does each group move?

steps.title: Synarthroses: immovable joints
teach: A suture joins bones with a thin layer of fibrous tissue, as in the skull. The tissue is left over from intramembranous ossification.
A syndesmosis connects bones with ligaments between them, like the radius and ulna, or the tibia and fibula. (Some authors call these amphiarthroses.)
A gomphosis is a cone-shaped process held in a socket by ligaments: a tooth in its alveolus, held by the periodontal ligament.

items.label: Radius and ulna joined by ligament

steps.title: Amphiarthroses: slightly movable joints
teach: A symphysis joins bones with a disk of fibrocartilage. The pubic symphysis gives a little during delivery to widen the birth canal.

A synchondrosis joins two bony surfaces with hyaline cartilage, later replaced by bone. Examples: the growth plate between the epiphysis and diaphysis of a long bone, and the rib-to-sternum cartilage. (Some authors call it a synarthrosis.)

items.label: Growth plate between epiphysis and diaphysis
Ribs joined to the sternum by cartilage

steps.title: Diarthroses: synovial joints
teach: Diarthroses (synovial joints) move freely. They always have a cavity enclosed by a capsule. Ligaments reinforce the capsule, articular cartilage covers the bone ends, and a synovial membrane lines the inside and makes synovial fluid. Most joints of the arms and legs are diarthroses.
Synovial fluid creates a smooth gliding surface for opposing bones and nourishes the articular cartilage, which has little blood supply.

Looser capsules allow more movement. The shoulder has the widest range; the hip is more restricted because its capsule is thicker and the femur is held in the acetabulum by strong ligaments. Muscles and tendons around the capsule add stability.

act.prompt: What provides a smooth gliding surface for opposing bones in a synovial joint?

options.label: Synovial fluid
options.feedback: Right. It also nourishes the cartilage.

steps.title: Movements: bending, straightening and side to side
teach: Flexion decreases the angle between bones (bending). Extension increases it (straightening). Hyperextension goes beyond anatomic position.
Abduction moves a bone away from the midline. Adduction moves it toward the midline.
Rotation turns a bone around its own axis, like shaking your head. Circumduction moves a limb so its end draws a circle and its sides draw a cone.

mnemonic.cue: ABduction ABducts it away; ADDuction ADDs it back
mnemonic.explanation: Abduction moves away from the midline; adduction brings it back to the body.

items.label: Raising your arm out to the side
Bringing your arm back to your side

steps.title: Movements of the hand, foot and jaw
teach: Supination turns the palm up (forearm bones parallel). Pronation turns the palm down (bones crossed). These are forearm and hand movements.
Eversion turns the sole of the foot outward; inversion turns it inward. Dorsiflexion raises the foot up at the ankle; plantar flexion pushes it down.

Protraction moves a part forward and retraction moves it back, like the jaw. Elevation raises a part and depression lowers it, like shrugging the shoulders. Opposition brings the thumb tip to the fingertips; it’s unique to primates. Reposition returns the digits.

mnemonic.cue: Supination = holding a bowl of SOUP
mnemonic.explanation: Palm up is supination; palm down is pronation.

act.prompt: Which part of the body does each movement belong to?

items.label: Dorsiflexion
items.feedback: Raising the foot at the ankle.

steps.title: Six types of synovial joints
teach: Ball-and-socket (multiaxial): a ball fits into a socket, giving the widest range of motion in all planes. Shoulder and hip; the shoulder moves more.
Hinge (uniaxial): flexion and extension in one plane. Elbow, knee, and the middle and distal finger and toe joints.
Pivot (uniaxial): rotation in one plane, like the atlas turning on the axis.
Condyloid or ellipsoidal (biaxial): an oval condyle in an elliptical cavity, moving in two planes. The wrist joint between the radius and carpals.
Saddle (biaxial): found only in the thumb, between the trapezium and the first metacarpal. It allows opposition.
Gliding (multiaxial): flat surfaces that only glide, like the joints between vertebral articular processes.

act.prompt: Match the joint to its type.

steps.title: Uniaxial, biaxial, multiaxial
teach: Joints are also named by how many planes they move in. Uniaxial: one plane (hinge, pivot). Biaxial: two planes at right angles (condyloid, saddle). Multiaxial: many planes (ball-and-socket; the textbook also calls gliding joints multiaxial).

steps.title: Bursae
teach: Bursae are closed sacs lined with synovial membrane, found wherever friction could happen between tendons, ligaments and bones.

Subcutaneous bursae are under the skin, over a bony process (like between the kneecap and the skin). Subfascial bursae are between muscles. Subtendinous bursae are where a tendon passes over another tendon or a bony projection, as in the shoulder.

items.label: Between the kneecap and the skin
Where a tendon passes over bone in the shoulder

steps.title: Joint disorders
teach: Arthritis is inflammation of the whole joint; there are over 100 kinds. Rheumatoid arthritis is a connective tissue disorder with severe inflammation of small joints, possibly autoimmune. Osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease) comes with age and affects weight-bearing joints. Gout is a build-up of uric acid crystals, often at the base of the big toe.
Bursitis is inflammation of a bursa. Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) comes from overuse. Carpal tunnel syndrome is a repetitive-motion injury of the wrist, common with keyboard use.

A sprain tears ligaments. A dislocation is a bone temporarily displaced from its joint. A slipped (herniated) disk presses on the spinal cord; if therapy fails, a laminectomy removes the protruding disk.

items.label: Uric acid crystals at the base of the big toe
Bone temporarily displaced from a joint

steps.title: Joints and aging
teach: With age, collagen and elastin in joints stiffen, cartilage wears faster than it’s replaced, and synovial fluid production drops, so range of motion decreases.
Moderate, regular exercise helps keep joints flexible.

act.prompt: Which change does the textbook link to stiffer joints with age?

options.label: Less synovial fluid and less flexible tendons and ligaments
More cartilage on the bone ends

flashcards.back: A joint: where two or more bones meet.
Freely movable synovial joints; most limb joints.
Bones joined by hyaline cartilage (growth plate).
Smooth gliding surface; nourishes articular cartilage.
Decrease / increase the angle between bones.
Limb end draws a circle; sides draw a cone.
Sole of the foot outward / inward.
Foot up / foot down at the ankle.
Under the skin over bony processes.
Uric acid crystals, often at the base of the big toe.
Surgical removal of a protruding disk.
A bone temporarily displaced from its joint.

quiz.q: Which joints do not allow movement?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says synarthroses are joints between bones that do not allow movement. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: The act of bending or decreasing the angle between bones is called _____________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 defines flexion as bending, or decreasing the angle between bones. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: An inflammation of the whole joint is called ___________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says arthritis is an inflammation of the whole joint. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: A bone that is moved away from the midline has undergone _____________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says abduction is moving a bone or limb away from the midline of the body. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: The femur is connected to the acetabulum by a series of strong ________________________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says the femur is connected to the acetabulum by a series of strong ligaments. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: A smooth gliding surface for opposing bones is provided by: ___________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says synovial fluid creates a smooth gliding surface for opposing bones. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Most joints of the upper and lower limbs are ______________________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says most joints of the upper and lower limbs are diarthroses. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: The elbow joint is an example of a _____________________ joint.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 gives the elbow and knee as examples of hinge joints. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: A __________________________ is the surgical removal of a protruding disk.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says a laminectomy is the surgical removal of the protruding disk. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Which movement involves raising the foot upward at the ankle joint?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says dorsiflexion is raising the foot up at the ankle joint. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: An example of a _____________________ is the joint between the epiphyses and the diaphysis of a long bone.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 gives the joint between the epiphyses and diaphysis of a long bone as an example of a synchondrosis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Subcutaneous bursae are found under the _____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says subcutaneous bursae are found under the skin wherever it lies over a bony process. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Eversion and inversion refer to movements of the _____________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says eversion and inversion refer to movements of the foot. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Which amphiarthrotic joints are characterized by two bony surfaces connected by hyaline cartilage?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says synchondroses are joints in which two bony surfaces are connected by hyaline cartilage. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: A temporarily displaced bone from a joint is called a _____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says a dislocation is a temporarily displaced bone from a joint. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Which type of joint is found only in the thumb?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says the saddle joint is found only in the thumb. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Which disease occurs when an accumulation of uric acid crystals accumulates in the joint at the base of the large toe and in other joints of the feet and legs?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says gout is an accumulation of uric acid crystals in the joint at the base of the large toe and other joints of the feet and legs. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: A ball-and-socket is an example of a(n) _____________________ joint.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says a ball-and-socket joint is an example of a multiaxial joint. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: The shoulder and hip are examples of _____________________ joints.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 gives the hip and shoulder as the two ball-and-socket joints. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Which type of arthritis is a connective tissue disorder resulting in severe inflammation of small joints?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says rheumatoid arthritis is a connective tissue disorder causing severe inflammation of small joints. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: The joints of the skull are examples of _____________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says the suture joints of the skull are examples of sutures. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Which injury is caused by repetitive movements that affect the wrist?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says carpal tunnel syndrome, affecting the wrist, develops from long periods of repetitive keyboard use. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Pronation is a term used to describe movement of the jaw.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Pronation is a movement of the forearm and hand (palm down). The jaw protracts and retracts. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: Extension increases the angle of bones.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 says extension is the act of increasing the angle between bones. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.

quiz.q: An example of an amphiarthrosis is a symphysis.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 8 lists the symphysis as one of the two examples of amphiarthroses. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 8.
